A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HyperPotter, with matching core methodology and identifiable correspondences across the main text and appendices. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HyperPotter evaluations, a retrained baseline, component ablations, codec-augmentation experiments, and representation analyses, including PartialSpoof case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds development-set replacement experiments, additional benchmark evaluations, O-information diagnostics, seed comparisons, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The backbone, FCM hyperedges, relational amplification, prototype initialization, alignment stages, and EMA updates are retained. Algorithm 1 and expanded operator and greedy-alignment descriptions provide additional implementation documentation without establishing a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds evaluations on varied speech patterns using EmoFake, MLAAD with MAILABS, and SingFake, plus a fake-only MLAAD evaluation. This broadens the evaluated data and scenarios beyond the retained 13-set suite. PartialSpoof was already used in v1 and is not a newly introduced dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Wav2Vec2+VIB with and without HAR, distinguishing HAR's additional resynthesized training data. Table 7 also includes VIB's MLAAD accuracy, while Figure 3 introduces an architecture-matched untrained control. The original detection comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds checkpoint-selection reruns using reported-disjoint, 2,000-sample PartialSpoof and ASVspoof5 development sets (Table 4), eight-second input evaluations (Table 16), accuracy for fake-only MLAAD, and new HOI and computational-cost evaluation procedures. The original four-second ASVspoof2019 LA training configuration remains the main setting.

E4.justification: New analyses test learned versus untrained O-information patterns, checkpoint-selection dependence, amplification transpose and normalization choices, FCM iteration sensitivity, computational scaling, and longer inputs. Table 9 also extends component ablations across all 13 original evaluation sets. Existing codec, SSL-front-end, convergence, and PartialSpoof analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 specifies seed 1234 and reports point estimates. v2 Table 15 reports both HyperPotter and baseline results for seeds 1234, 1111, and 4321 on five datasets, together with means and standard deviations. This introduces substantive repeated-run and uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original benchmark EER and F1 values remain unchanged, but substantial new results appear throughout the appendices. Examples include EmoFake EERs of 1.40% versus the baseline's 2.01%, and eight-second 21LA EERs of 2.04% versus 4.10%. The conclusion's former 15.32% average-gain figure is replaced with explicitly defined relative EER reductions of 12.68% across all 13 sets and 22.15% across the 11 improved sets.

T1.justification: Appendix F.2 adds time and memory complexity derivations, and Appendix B.3 defines centroid-based variables and label-relevant O-information gain. Section 5.3 replaces the optimal-permutation expression with an explicit greedy assignment formulation. These are bounded formal additions and corrections; the principal entropy, FCM, amplification, and EMA equations remain.

C1.justification: The central claim is narrowed from demonstrating synergy-dominated synthetic artifacts to providing suggestive evidence of structured redundancy-synergy patterns. Claims of consistent generalization become explicit improvements on 11 of 13 sets with codec/channel limitations. The abstract and conclusion distinguish overall gains from gains on the improved subset, while retaining the HyperPotter contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits O-information to a diagnostic interpretation rather than a formal decomposition into pure redundancy or synergy. It acknowledges that removing components can improve codec-heavy results, proposes adapting the redundancy-synergy balance, and discusses efficiency, stability, and longer-input tradeoffs. The codec-masking hypothesis itself was already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 supplies detailed HAGNN pseudocode, hyperparameter provenance, exact cluster configurations, checkpoint epochs, the 2,000-sample ITW selection disclosure, and operational details for new diagnostics and timing experiments. It specifies the cost-measurement hardware and batch sizes and replaces the anonymous code/model access reference with a GitHub repository reference.

R1.justification: Targeted citations are added for VIB comparisons, HOI diagnostics, information-bottleneck motivation, incremental deepfake learning, and graph augmentation. Examples include Doan et al. (2024), Urbina-Rodriguez et al. (2026), and Pan et al. (2023). The overall related-work structure and hypergraph/prototype positioning remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, information-theoretic exposition, amplification explanation, and conclusion receive substantive rewrites. Appendices A–I are reorganized into A–F with thematic subsections, and Discussion, Acknowledgements, and Impact Statement sections are added. This substantially revises the narrative and document organization.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout. Retained figures are resized and relocated, while new trained/untrained heatmaps, an algorithm display, expanded comparison tables, and several new experimental tables substantially change the presentation. Existing appendix plots remain identifiable despite renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation that previously relied on ITW-based checkpoint selection and one reported seed. Alternative development-set experiments (Table 4), seed uncertainty (Table 15), trained/untrained HOI diagnostics, and detailed implementation and cost reporting address important evidential and reproducibility gaps. The revised headline claims also better reflect the retained results. The main scores still use ITW-based selection and the synergy interpretation remains suggestive, but the added controls and qualifications materially improve the paper's credibility.
